Clean pass with disclosed caveats. SOURCE: Queiros A, Fernandes E, Reniers R, Sampaio A, Coutinho J, Seara-Cardoso A (2018) PLOS ONE 13(6):e0197755, CC BY 4.0. The study's own S1 File (article/file?type=supplementary&id=10.1371/journal.pone.0197755.s001, sha256 df58fd40962878041e75972832175ceb4cfc8f0aea5f3a9daf8baa169e2d2d8b) is headed 'Portuguese Version of the QCAE (Questionario de Empatia Afetiva e Cognitiva)' and prints all 31 Portuguese items NUMBERED 1..31, plus the instructions and the four anchor labels. ADMINISTERED LANGUAGE: the administered Portuguese is shipped in item_text / instructions / option_text and English sits in the _translated columns, per the 2026-09-01 rule; language=Portuguese. MAPPING: the IRW item codes ARE the source .xls column names -- data/queiros_2018_qcae.py melts ITEM_COLS = QCAE_1..QCAE_31 unchanged, no positional or renaming step -- so the only claim to test is that column QCAE_<n> is the S1 File's item <n>. That is a number match published by the study itself, hence paper_explicit rather than paper_order. It is independently corroborated by the sibling deposit gomez_2022_qcae, whose SPSS variable labels carry the numbered English items ('15. I can easily tell if someone else wants to enter a conversation.'): every one of the 31 Portuguese items is a translation of the English item bearing the same number. REVERSE ITEMS AND WHAT THE IRW TABLE STORES: the source .xls also ships QCAE_1_R/2_R/17_R/29_R (verified here to equal 5 - QCAE_1/2/17/29 for all 562 respondents); the IRW build drops them, so this table holds only RAW, unreversed scores for all 31 items and resp 1..4 means the same thing on every item. option_text is therefore uniform: 1 = 'Discordo Fortemente' ... 4 = 'Concordo Fortemente'. That direction is stated by the paper ('a 4-point Likert scale ranging from strongly disagree (1) to strongly agree (4)') and confirmed numerically (see verification sidecar). ITEM 17: the paper drops item 17 from every published composite 'due to an extremely low loading value', leaving a three-item Peripheral Responsivity subscale (items 2, 11, 29). It is present in this table, and in the data it is the one item essentially unrelated to its own subscale (item-rest r = -0.03). Nothing was altered; this is a property of the source study, recorded so a user does not assume a canonical four-item PeR. TRANSCRIPTION DEVIATIONS: the S1 File's leading item numbering ('1. ') and the non-breaking space after it were stripped; nothing else was altered, so the source's own missing terminal full stops (every item) are kept as-is. The two instruction sentences of the S1 File were joined into one instructions string. section_prompt blank (single trivial section, no testlets). correct_response blank (attitude scale). TRANSLATION PROVENANCE (why translation_source=mixed): item_text_translated and option_text_translated are the QCAE originators' own English for the same numbered items -- Reniers RLEP, Corcoran R, Drake R, Shryane NM, Vollm BA (2011) J Pers Assess 93(1):84-95 -- taken verbatim from the already-shipped gomez_2022_qcae table, 27 of whose items came from that deposit's numbered SPSS variable labels; so those two fields are official_instrument_english. instructions_translated is NOT: no published English exists for this Portuguese adaptation's instruction sentences, so that ONE field is an IRW rendering of the Portuguese, i.e. machine_translation. It is disclosed in public_note. STEP 3b: table name, dictionary Description and live content all agree -- 31 items, resp 1-4, 562 respondents, and the S1 File's instrument is the QCAE. This deposit contains no other instrument. RIGHTS -- SHIP-SHAPED, ESCALATED, NO REGISTER ROW WRITTEN (per the 2026-09-10 rule that a round may write a block row but never a ship row). No clause reserving a right could be located from the instrument's rights holder. What exists: (i) a bare copyright notice attached to the Reniers et al. (2011) J Pers Assess appendix -- 'The QCAE is copyrighted by the authors. Permission has been granted to Taylor and Francis to reproduce the item content' -- which reserves nothing beyond copyright itself and is not a block under the 2026-09-05 test; (ii) Taylor & Francis's standard per-article Terms & Conditions boilerplate ('This article may be used for research, teaching and private study purposes. Any substantial or systematic reproduction... is expressly forbidden'), which is the publisher's term for the ARTICLE FILE, not the rights holder's term for the instrument, and no wording here was copied from that PDF; (iii) a third-party catalogue entry (UNSW Social Cognition resources, sha256 8669d524401e1d5263d0878cf2ee2deff765673127e8641ebd28d481feccf6aa) whose 'How to obtain' field reads 'Available from the authors' -- a description of where to get the form on someone else's page, not a clause by the originator. Weighing the other way, and specific to this table: the Portuguese wording actually shipped in the base fields was published in full under CC BY 4.0 by a paper whose author list INCLUDES Renate Reniers, the QCAE's originator, so the originator herself put this derivative under an open licence.
